review_notes: I read the whole file. I also looked at the three places that use `balanced_of_strongEpiCategory` (lines 256, 322, 487) and the two proofs that use `pushforward_closedIncl_stalk_eq_zero` in an epi argument. I did not check the other proofs in detail. I judged the repeated `Functor.map_isIso` / `IsIso.comp_isIso` steps in `closedIncl_unit_stalk_isIso` to be short routine API calls, so I did not report them. The suggested lemma has not been compiled. The defeq identification of `(pushforward i).obj G` with the presheaf pushforward of `G.obj`, which both uses need, is assumed to hold by `rfl`/`change`. The other proofs here already rely on the same identification.

findings.declaration: epi_pushforward_map_closedIncl_of_locallySurjective and epi_unit_of_closedImmersion (shared skeleton: Balanced instance, epi ↔ locally surjective ↔ stalkwise surjective, case split on x ∈ s, zero-stalk branch)
findings.problem: Both proofs show that a morphism of sheaves into a closed-immersion pushforward is epi, and they use the same argument. They obtain `Balanced` from `balanced_of_strongEpiCategory`, rewrite with `isLocallySurjective_iff_epi` and `locally_surjective_iff_surjective_on_stalks`, then split on `x ∈ s`. For `x ∉ s` they use `pushforward_closedIncl_stalk_eq_zero` to show every element of the target stalk is 0, hence in the image. The only real work is the `x ∈ s` branch. The same `Balanced` instance is also built in `closedIncl_pushforward_preservesEpis` (line 322). The argument is spelled out twice, with long explicit terms.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma after `pushforward_closedIncl_stalk_eq_zero`, for example `epi_of_stalk_surjective_on_closed`. Take `hs : IsClosed s`, a sheaf `A` on `X`, a sheaf `G` on `TopCat.of s`, a morphism `φ : A ⟶ (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward AddCommGrpCat (TopCat.closedIncl hs)).obj G`, and a hypothesis `h : ∀ z : TopCat.of s, Function.Surjective ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat ((TopCat.closedIncl hs) z)).map φ.hom)`. The conclusion is `Epi φ`. The proof is the current skeleton: introduce `Balanced`, rewrite to stalkwise surjectivity, and split on `x ∈ s`. The `x ∈ s` case applies `h ⟨x, hx⟩`. The `x ∉ s` case is `fun b ↦ ⟨0, by rw [pushforward_closedIncl_stalk_eq_zero hs G.property hx b]; exact map_zero _⟩`. Then `epi_unit_of_closedImmersion` reduces to `epi_of_stalk_surjective_on_closed hZ _ (fun z ↦ (ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso _).2)`, using `closedIncl_unit_stalk_isIso`. The `x ∈ s` branch of `epi_pushforward_map_closedIncl_of_locallySurjective` keeps only its stalk-naturality and `stalkPushforward` isomorphism argument, which proves the `h` hypothesis for `pushforward.map fsh`. The `Balanced` instance would also be built only once, inside the lemma.
findings.benefit: The case split and the vanishing of stalks off the closed set, which is the main idea of the closed-immersion epi argument, is stated and proved once. Each use then only proves surjectivity of stalk maps at points of `s`. Any change to the sheaf/stalk API (for example `Balanced`, or the coercion between `Sheaf.pushforward` and `Presheaf.pushforward`) then needs fixing in one place, not in two proofs plus the instance.
